acceptanceCovered: /login is reachable while the prelaunch launch gate is locked, and renders the header logo, language selector, ROOT FURTHER hero, intro copy, LOGIN With Google button and copyright footer — proven by e2e/login-screen.spec.ts assertions A1 through A7 and A12 passing against the port-3000 locked-gate server, plus orchestrator browser captures at 1440 and 375 in this directory

Clicking the login button initiates Google OAuth via Supabase authorize with provider=google and a redirect_to pointing at /auth/callback, in the same tab — proven by assertion A8 intercepting the authorize request and asserting provider, redirect_to and a single open page

The login button is disabled and reports aria-busy while authentication is in flight — proven by assertion A9 after the intercept was changed to fulfil with HTTP 204, asserting toBeDisabled and aria-busy=true conjunctively
A failed or cancelled authentication renders the fixed Vietnamese error string in a role=alert region — proven by assertion A10 loading /login?error=access_denied and asserting the role=alert text

An already-authenticated visitor to /login is redirected to / — proven by e2e/login-auth-redirect.spec.ts assertion A11 against the port-3200 open-gate server with a seeded signInWithPassword session, asserting the exact origin root

/login and /auth/callback are exempt from the prelaunch launch gate in both the locked and unlocked directions, and the gate remains launch-timing only, never authorization — proven by lib/prelaunch/gate.test.ts locked, unlocked and invalid-config cases plus near-miss guards, and by reviewer confirmation that no auth awareness reached gate.ts

Supabase session refresh is merged into the single Next 16 proxy.ts and refreshed auth cookies survive a gate redirect rather than being silently dropped — proven by reading proxy.ts, where updateSupabaseSession returns supabaseCookies alongside the response and every cookie is copied onto the gate redirect before it ships

No secret key is reachable from client code, getUser is used in every server context rather than getSession, and no real credential is committed — proven by greps returning no getSession and no secret-key reference under app, lib or components, and by git ls-files showing only .env.example tracked
regressionChecked: 56 pre-existing E2E tests across homepage, prelaunch, dropdown, navigation and invalid-env suites still pass unchanged after the proxy.ts merge that runs on every request
lib/prelaunch/gate.test.ts grew from 40 to 55 to 57 cases additively; the diff is insertions-only, so no prior launch-gate assertion was weakened or removed
The shared i18n dictionaries gained only login.* keys; every existing screen consuming them still renders and passes its suite
npm run lint exits clean and the only ignore added is the supabase/.temp generated artifact, verified to be the sole source of all 182 prior errors so no real finding was hidden
lib/session/session-provider.tsx is byte-unchanged, so the mock-session behaviour every existing screen depends on is untouched by the new auth boundary

findings.summary: Callback redirects were built from request.nextUrl.origin, which Next derives from the incoming Host header, making this unauthenticated internet-reachable route an open redirect behind infrastructure that does not pin Host. Fixed by resolving every redirect against a canonical NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL via getSiteUrl().

ALWAYS_ALLOWED prefix matching was correct but untested for near-misses, so a future refactor to a bare startsWith would silently exempt /loginX from the launch gate. Added regression guards asserting /loginX and /auth/callbackX still redirect while locked.

Login_Keyvisual.png is 468 KB with no WebP or AVIF variant and no smaller source for sm and md widths. Deferred: it is already down from 2.2 MB, and the real remedy is a clean layer export from the design owner, which is a tracked follow-up.

When signInWithOAuth returns an error object rather than throwing, the underlying Supabase message is discarded and only a boolean surfaces. Deferred: this is the recorded BR-002 behaviour, and a future maintainer debugging a silent failure has nothing to grep.
A very fast double click can re-enter handleClick in the window before React commits the disabled attribute. Deferred: signInWithOAuth navigates away immediately and the practical risk is negligible.
